headline: The packs now stand in the corridor
lede: TEN-DEEP's ambushes stopped being hidden tiles: every live pack shows up in the 3D dungeon as lit, tinted, shambling billboards — and the pixels prove the monster you see is the monster that takes your step.

notes.text: POLISH — TEN-DEEP (#2318 → PR #2322): mobview.js derives one billboard per living mob from live sim state — whole bestiary covered on the atlas with per-mob tint/size, the Hollow King and his wyrm wardens standing at the throne beacon. Offsets clamp inside the den tile, so sight and trigger always agree; depth-testing hides packs around corners; spent groups vanish. The sim rule never moved — solver, campaign proof, slack and determinism re-ran untouched.

tendeepcheck 10279/10279 with five new mutants dying (loose offsets, lingering packs, dropped wardens, emptied corridor, unwired tint); tendepplay 92/92 — bone-white bodies light 1363 px at a fixed pose and drop to 0 px once the pack is spent.

The shared renderer's own comment promised sprite `tint` since #1129 — the shader never read it. uTint is wired now (white default, deepglass byte-identical), so three atlas shapes read as ten bestiary members.

PLAICRAFT S1 (#1711) re-checked and released: store unchanged, all builder lines shipped and graded; waiting on Jon's clap-test take at /retrogames/claptest and the SESSION_WRITE_KEY deploy (jonq #2305).

look.text: Walk TEN-DEEP's first corridors and see the rats before they see you
